links.outcome: Model performance on external test sets from same and different OCT machines
links.effect: FMUE achieved similar excellent performance on two external test sets from the same and different OCT machines.
links.quote: The model achieves similar excellent performance on two external test sets from the same and different OCT machines.

links.outcome: F1 score of AI versus clinicians and GPT-4V on OCT diagnosis
links.effect: FMUE F1 96.30% vs retinal experts 86.95% (p=0.004), senior doctors 82.71%, junior doctors 66.55%, GPT-4V 32.39% (all p<0.001).
links.quote: In human-model comparison, FMUE achieves a higher F1 score of 96.30% than retinal experts (86.95%, p = 0.004), senior doctors (82.71%, p < 0.001), junior doctors (66.55%, p < 0.001), and generative pretrained transformer 4 with vision (GPT-4V) (32.39%, p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Uncertainty scores flagging out-of-scope or low-quality images for manual check
links.effect: FMUE predicts high uncertainty scores for >85% of images of non-target-category diseases or with low quality, prompting manual checks.
links.quote: Besides, FMUE predicts high uncertainty scores for >85% images of non-target-category diseases or with low quality to prompt manual checks and prevent misdiagnosis.

unlisted_practices: Uncertainty estimation with a threshold strategy to flag unseen disease classes and improve F1 (95.74% to 97.44%)

screen.reason: The study develops and evaluates a foundation model with uncertainty estimation (FMUE) for OCT diagnosis, testing uncertainty thresholding to prompt manual checks and prevent misdiagnosis of out-of-distribution/low-quality images.

primary.practice: uncertainty estimation thresholding for manual review escalation
